seed_attach() {
    # Serialize shared-seed alias registration across identities. Keep this
    # stable host lock separate from per-identity receipts/Cozo authority.
    seed_shared_lock
    # Same-boot missing/reassigned mappings require operator inspection.
    # Cross-boot receipts are cleared only by seed_load's verified cold gate.
    if [ -n "$seed_view" ]; then
        seed_verify_loop "$seed_view" "$seed_device" 1
    else
        # Deliberately do NOT use --nooverlap: each identity owns a distinct
        # read-only block-device view of the SAME partition, with no copies.
        seed_view=$(losetup --find --show --read-only --loop-ref "seed:$native_uuid" "$seed_device")
        seed_record_loops
    fi
    if [ -n "$leaf_loop" ]; then
        seed_verify_loop "$leaf_loop" "$leaf" 0
    else
        [ -z "$(losetup -j "$leaf" -n -O NAME)" ] || seed_fail "leaf already mapped outside its receipt"
        leaf_loop=$(losetup --find --show --loop-ref "leaf:$native_uuid" "$leaf")
        seed_record_loops
    fi
    [ "$seed_view" != "$leaf_loop" ] || seed_fail "identical seed and leaf devices"
}
seed_verify_volume() {
    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$seed_dir/volume" -o FSTYPE)" = btrfs ] &&
        [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$seed_dir/volume" -o FSROOT)" = / ] &&
        [ "$(seed_super "$leaf_loop")" = "$sprout_fsid" ] || seed_fail "unexpected sprout mount"
    members=$(btrfs filesystem show --raw "$seed_dir/volume")
    printf '%s\n' "$members" | grep -q "uuid: $sprout_fsid" || seed_fail "mounted FSID differs"
    [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$members" | awk '$1 == "devid" {n++} END {print n+0}')" = 2 ] || seed_fail "unexpected sprout member count"
    actual_members=$(printf '%s\n' "$members" | awk '$1 == "devid" {print $NF}' | sort)
    expected_members=$(printf '%s\n' "$seed_view" "$leaf_loop" | sort)
    [ "$actual_members" = "$expected_members" ] || seed_fail "sprout members differ from own loop receipts"
}
seed_member_pin() {
    [ -d "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] || seed_fail "missing or unsafe sibling subvolume: $1"
    pin_show=$(btrfs subvolume show "$1") || seed_fail "not a subvolume: $1"
    pin_id=$(printf '%s\n' "$pin_show" | awk '$1 == "Subvolume" && $2 == "ID:" {print $3}')
    pin_uuid=$(printf '%s\n' "$pin_show" | awk '$1 == "UUID:" {print $2}')
    printf '%s' "$pin_id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+$' && [ "$pin_id" -gt 5 ] && valid_session "$pin_uuid" || seed_fail "invalid sibling subvolume identity"

seed_layout_pins() {
    # Listing at subvolid=5 includes nested members. Do not merely check that
    # the seven expected names exist: reject every extra or nested subvolume.
    subvolume_listing=$(btrfs subvolume list "$seed_dir/volume") || seed_fail "cannot enumerate seed subvolumes"

    expected_subvolumes=$(printf '%s\n' @ @agent_memory @agent_rules @agent_shared @agent_skills @agent_soul @agent_user | LC_ALL=C sort)
    [ "$actual_subvolumes" = "$expected_subvolumes" ] || seed_fail "seed must contain exactly seven flat sibling subvolumes"

    pins='{}'
    for sibling in @ @agent_memory @agent_rules @agent_shared @agent_skills @agent_soul @agent_user; do
        pin=$(seed_member_pin "$seed_dir/volume/$sibling") || seed_fail "cannot pin sibling: $sibling"
        pins=$(printf '%s\n' "$pins" | jq -c --arg member "$sibling" --argjson pin "$pin" '. + {($member):$pin}') || seed_fail "cannot record sibling pin"
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$pins" | jq -ce 'select(([.[].id] | unique | length) == 7 and ([.[].uuid] | unique | length) == 7)'

seed_persist_pin() {
    persist_parent=$seed_dir/volume/@agent_user
    persist_dir=$persist_parent/persist
    parent_pin=$(seed_member_pin "$persist_parent") || seed_fail "invalid persistence parent"
    [ -d "$persist_dir" ] && [ ! -L "$persist_dir" ] &&
        [ "$(stat -c %a "$persist_dir")" = 700 ] || seed_fail "unsafe ordinary persistence directory"
    ! btrfs subvolume show "$persist_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1 || seed_fail "persistence must not be a subvolume"
    ! mountpoint -q "$persist_dir" || seed_fail "persistence source must not be a separate mount"
    [ "$(stat -c %d "$persist_dir")" = "$(stat -c %d "$persist_parent")" ] || seed_fail "persistence is not on its parent filesystem"

seed_verify_layout() {
    [ "$(seed_image_metadata | jq -cS .)" = "$(jq -cS '.image' "$seed_dir/state.json")" ] || seed_fail "pinned image metadata changed"
    actual_pins=$(seed_layout_pins) || seed_fail "invalid shared sibling layout"

    [ "$(seed_persist_pin | jq -cS .)" = "$(jq -cS '.persist' "$seed_dir/state.json")" ] || seed_fail "private persistence directory or parent identity changed"
    for sibling in @ @agent_memory @agent_rules @agent_shared @agent_skills @agent_soul @agent_user; do
        case "$sibling" in @agent_rules|@agent_shared|@agent_soul) readonly=true ;; *) readonly=false ;; esac
        [ "$(btrfs property get -ts "$seed_dir/volume/$sibling" ro)" = "ro=$readonly" ] || seed_fail "sibling protection changed: $sibling"
    done

seed_bind_member() {

        [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$member_root" -o FSROOT)" = "/${member_source#"$seed_dir/volume/"}" ] || seed_fail "guest member mount source changed"
    case ",$(findmnt -rn -M "$member_root" -o VFS-OPTIONS)," in
        *,ro,*) [ "$member_readonly" = true ] || seed_fail "private member is mounted read-only" ;;
        *) [ "$member_readonly" = false ] || seed_fail "protected member is writable" ;;
    esac

seed_mount_guest() {

    seed_verify_layout
    guest=$seed_dir/volume/@
    [ -d "$guest/agent" ] && [ ! -L "$guest/agent" ] || seed_fail "guest agent parent is not an ordinary directory"

seed_attach() {
    # Serialize shared-seed alias registration across identities. Keep this
    # stable host lock separate from per-identity receipts/Cozo authority.
    seed_shared_lock
    # Same-boot missing/reassigned mappings require operator inspection.
    # Cross-boot receipts are cleared only by seed_load's verified cold gate.
    if [ -n "$seed_view" ]; then
        seed_verify_loop "$seed_view" "$seed_device" 1
    else
        # Deliberately do NOT use --nooverlap: each identity owns a distinct
        # read-only block-device view of the SAME partition, with no copies.
        seed_view=$(losetup --find --show --read-only --loop-ref "seed:$native_uuid" "$seed_device")
        seed_record_loops
    fi
    if [ -n "$leaf_loop" ]; then
        seed_verify_loop "$leaf_loop" "$leaf" 0
    else
        [ -z "$(losetup -j "$leaf" -n -O NAME)" ] || seed_fail "leaf already mapped outside its receipt"
        leaf_loop=$(losetup --find --show --loop-ref "leaf:$native_uuid" "$leaf")
        seed_record_loops
    fi
    [ "$seed_view" != "$leaf_loop" ] || seed_fail "identical seed and leaf devices"
}
seed_verify_volume() {
    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$seed_dir/volume" -o FSTYPE)" = btrfs ] &&
        [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$seed_dir/volume" -o FSROOT)" = / ] &&
        [ "$(seed_super "$leaf_loop")" = "$sprout_fsid" ] || seed_fail "unexpected sprout mount"
    members=$(btrfs filesystem show --raw "$seed_dir/volume")
    printf '%s\n' "$members" | grep -q "uuid: $sprout_fsid" || seed_fail "mounted FSID differs"

    actual_members=$(printf '%s\n' "$members" | awk '$1 == "devid" {print $NF}' | sort)

seed_member_pin() {

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Bind the already prepared chatbot sprout. No format, member change or start.
set -euo pipefail
fail() { printf 'bind-instance-root: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ $# == 1 && $1 == 3tchedChatbot && $(id -u) == 0 ]] || fail 'usage: bind-instance-root 3tchedChatbot (host root)'
incus() { command incus --force-local "$@"; }
umask 077
name=$1
pool=/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool
disk=$pool/.provisioning/$name.json
receipt=$pool/.provisioning/$name.incus.json
[[ ! -L $disk && -f $disk && ! -L $receipt && -f $receipt ]] || fail 'operator preparation receipts required'
exec 9>"$pool/.provisioning/$name.lock"
flock -n 9 || fail 'instance preparation active'
jq -e '.phase=="filesystems-prepared" and .filesystem_prepared==true' "$disk" >/dev/null || fail 'filesystems not prepared'
jq -e '.phase=="container-defined" and .identity_registered==false and .root_bound==false' "$receipt" >/dev/null || fail 'existing root intent requires manual reconciliation'
root=$pool/.mounts/$name/root
replica=$pool/.mounts/$name/upgrade
view=$pool/.mounts/$name/root-view
seed_layer=$pool/.mounts/$name/seed-layer
upgrade_layer=$pool/.mounts/$name/upgrade-layer
container_root=/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/identity-roots/containers/$name/rootfs
sid=b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28
image=$pool/$name.img
[[ $(findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSROOT) == /@3tched-leaf-pool &&
   $(jq -r .image "$disk") == "$image" && -f $image && ! -L $image &&
   $(stat -c %i "$image") == "$(jq -r .image_inode "$disk")" &&
   $(stat -c %s "$image") == "$(jq -r .image_bytes "$disk")" &&
   $(jq -r .root_mount "$disk") == "$root" &&
   $(findmnt -rn -M "$root" -o FSTYPE) == btrfs &&
   $(findmnt -rn -M "$root" -o FSROOT) == / ]] || fail 'prepared root/image pins differ'
root_source=$(findmnt -rn -M "$root" -o SOURCE)
[[ $(blkid -p -s UUID -o value "$root_source") == "$(jq -r .root_fsid "$disk")" ]] || fail 'wrong sprout filesystem'
pair=$pool/.provisioning/$name.upgrade.json
[[ -f $pair && ! -L $pair ]] || fail 'upgrade pair must be established during provisioning'
jq -e --arg replica "$(jq -r .upgrade_fsid "$disk")" '.phase=="paired" and
    .host_fsid=="5a88e7cd-9701-40a7-8301-ef076761886c" and .replica_fsid==$replica and
    .direction=="host-to-container"' "$pair" >/dev/null || fail 'upgrade pair differs'
[[ $(findmnt -rn -M "$replica" -o FSTYPE) == btrfs &&
   $(findmnt -rn -M "$replica" -o FSROOT) == / ]] || fail 'upgrade filesystem not mounted'
for layer in "$view" "$seed_layer" "$upgrade_layer"; do
    [[ ! -L $layer && -z $(findmnt -rn -M "$layer") ]] || fail 'retained OS view requires reconciliation'
done
instance=$(incus query "/1.0/instances/$name")
jq -e --arg sid "$sid" '.status=="Stopped" and .config["user.opdbus.session_id"]==$sid and
   .config["security.privileged"]=="false" and .config["security.protection.shift"]=="true" and
   .devices.root.pool=="identity-roots" and .profiles==["3tched-lungs"]' <<<"$instance" >/dev/null || fail 'stopped container binding differs'
idmap=$(jq -er '.config["volatile.idmap.current"]' <<<"$instance")
jq -e 'length==2 and all(.[]; .Hostid==1000000 and .Nsid==0 and .Maprange==1000000000) and
    any(.[]; .Isuid==true and .Isgid==false) and any(.[]; .Isgid==true and .Isuid==false)' <<<"$idmap" >/dev/null || fail 'unsupported container idmap'
[[ ! -L $container_root && -d $container_root && $(realpath -e "$container_root") == "$container_root" &&
   -z $(findmnt -rn -M "$container_root") && ! -L $root/@/etc/fstab && -f $root/@/etc/fstab &&
   ! -L $root/@/etc/hostname && -f $root/@/etc/hostname ]] || fail 'unexpected root mount or guest configuration'
for member in memory rules shared skills soul user; do
    [[ -d $root/@/agent/$member && ! -L $root/@/agent/$member &&
       -d $root/@agent_$member && ! -L $root/@agent_$member ]] || fail 'missing ordinary mountpoint or sibling'
    btrfs subvolume show "$root/@agent_$member" >/dev/null
done
# Keep the Incus empty-root scaffolding underneath the bind; never delete it.
[[ ! -e $pool/.provisioning/$name.before-root.json ]] || fail 'retained container backup requires reconciliation'
printf '%s\n' "$instance" > "$pool/.provisioning/$name.before-root.json"
cp -a "$root/@/etc/fstab" "$pool/.provisioning/$name.fstab.before"
jq '.phase="root-bind-intent"' "$receipt" > "$receipt.new"
sync -f "$receipt.new"
mv -T "$receipt.new" "$receipt"
for device in 3tchedfs system-bus; do
    if jq -e --arg device "$device" '.devices|has($device)' <<<"$instance" >/dev/null; then
        incus config device remove "$name" "$device"
    fi
done
if jq -e '.devices|has("fuse")' <<<"$instance" >/dev/null; then
    jq -e '.devices.fuse=={type:"unix-char",source:"/dev/fuse",path:"/dev/fuse"}' <<<"$instance" >/dev/null || fail 'different fuse device'
else
    incus config device add "$name" fuse unix-char source=/dev/fuse path=/dev/fuse
fi
printf '%s\n' '# Container root and agent subvolumes are mounted by the external identity mount owner.' \
    '# Do not mount the physical seed or host boot partitions inside this container.' > "$root/@/etc/fstab"
printf '%s\n' "$sid" > "$root/@/etc/hostname"
incus config set "$name" "volatile.last_state.idmap=$idmap"
sync -f "$root"
mkdir -p "$view" "$seed_layer" "$upgrade_layer"
mount --bind -o ro,X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$root/@" "$seed_layer"
mount --bind -o ro,X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$replica/@" "$upgrade_layer"
mount -t overlay overlay -o "ro,lowerdir=$upgrade_layer:$seed_layer" "$view"
mount --bind "$view" "$container_root"
for member in memory rules shared skills soul user; do
    mount --bind -o X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$root/@agent_$member" "$container_root/agent/$member"
    case "$member" in shared|soul) mount -o remount,bind,ro "$container_root/agent/$member" ;; esac
done
mount --bind -o X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$root/@agent_user/persist" "$container_root/opt/run-mounts/persist"
instance=$(incus query "/1.0/instances/$name")
jq --arg root "$container_root" --arg view "$view" --argjson instance "$instance" \
   '.phase="root-bound"|.root_bound=true|.threetched_root=$root|.instance=$instance|
    .root_view=$view|.root_view_readonly=true|.upgrade_paired=true|
    .guest_fuse_configured=true|.guest_fuse_mounted=false|.host_fuse_mirrored=false' "$receipt" > "$receipt.new"
sync -f "$receipt.new"
mv -T "$receipt.new" "$receipt"
sync -f "$pool/.provisioning"
printf 'Existing root bound; container stopped, identity adoption and live guest FUSE remain pending.\n'

seed_attach() {
    # Serialize shared-seed alias registration across identities. Keep this
    # stable host lock separate from per-identity receipts/Cozo authority.
    seed_shared_lock
    # Same-boot missing/reassigned mappings require operator inspection.
    # Cross-boot receipts are cleared only by seed_load's verified cold gate.
    if [ -n "$seed_view" ]; then
        seed_verify_loop "$seed_view" "$seed_device" 1
    else
        # Deliberately do NOT use --nooverlap: each identity owns a distinct
        # read-only block-device view of the SAME partition, with no copies.
        seed_view=$(losetup --find --show --read-only --loop-ref "seed:$native_uuid" "$seed_device")
        seed_record_loops
    fi
    if [ -n "$leaf_loop" ]; then
        seed_verify_loop "$leaf_loop" "$leaf" 0
    else
        [ -z "$(losetup -j "$leaf" -n -O NAME)" ] || seed_fail "leaf already mapped outside its receipt"
        leaf_loop=$(losetup --find --show --loop-ref "leaf:$native_uuid" "$leaf")
        seed_record_loops
    fi
    [ "$seed_view" != "$leaf_loop" ] || seed_fail "identical seed and leaf devices"
}
seed_verify_volume() {
    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$seed_dir/volume" -o FSTYPE)" = btrfs ] &&
        [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$seed_dir/volume" -o FSROOT)" = / ] &&
        [ "$(seed_super "$leaf_loop")" = "$sprout_fsid" ] || seed_fail "unexpected sprout mount"
    members=$(btrfs filesystem show --raw "$seed_dir/volume")
    printf '%s\n' "$members" | grep -q "uuid: $sprout_fsid" || seed_fail "mounted FSID differs"
    [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$members" | awk '$1 == "devid" {n++} END {print n+0}')" = 2 ] || seed_fail "unexpected sprout member count"
    actual_members=$(printf '%s\n' "$members" | awk '$1 == "devid" {print $NF}' | sort)
    expected_members=$(printf '%s\n' "$seed_view" "$leaf_loop" | sort)
    [ "$actual_members" = "$expected_members" ] || seed_fail "sprout members differ from own loop receipts"
}
seed_member_pin() {
    [ -d "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] || seed_fail "missing or unsafe sibling subvolume: $1"
    pin_show=$(btrfs subvolume show "$1") || seed_fail "not a subvolume: $1"
    pin_id=$(printf '%s\n' "$pin_show" | awk '$1 == "Subvolume" && $2 == "ID:" {print $3}')
    pin_uuid=$(printf '%s\n' "$pin_show" | awk '$1 == "UUID:" {print $2}')
    printf '%s' "$pin_id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+$' && [ "$pin_id" -gt 5 ] && valid_session "$pin_uuid" || seed_fail "invalid sibling subvolume identity"
    jq -cn --arg id "$pin_id" --arg uuid "$pin_uuid" '{id:$id,uuid:$uuid}'
}
seed_layout_pins() {
    # Listing at subvolid=5 includes nested members. Do not merely check that
    # the seven expected names exist: reject every extra or nested subvolume.
    subvolume_listing=$(btrfs subvolume list "$seed_dir/volume") || seed_fail "cannot enumerate seed subvolumes"
    actual_subvolumes=$(printf '%s\n' "$subvolume_listing" | sed -n 's/^.* path //p' | LC_ALL=C sort)
    expected_subvolumes=$(printf '%s\n' @ @agent_memory @agent_rules @agent_shared @agent_skills @agent_soul @agent_user | LC_ALL=C sort)
    [ "$actual_subvolumes" = "$expected_subvolumes" ] || seed_fail "seed must contain exactly seven flat sibling subvolumes"
    [ ! -e "$seed_dir/volume/@persist" ] && [ ! -L "$seed_dir/volume/@persist" ] || seed_fail "old extra persistence subvolume/layout is unsupported"
    pins='{}'
    for sibling in @ @agent_memory @agent_rules @agent_shared @agent_skills @agent_soul @agent_user; do
        pin=$(seed_member_pin "$seed_dir/volume/$sibling") || seed_fail "cannot pin sibling: $sibling"
        pins=$(printf '%s\n' "$pins" | jq -c --arg member "$sibling" --argjson pin "$pin" '. + {($member):$pin}') || seed_fail "cannot record sibling pin"
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$pins" | jq -ce 'select(([.[].id] | unique | length) == 7 and ([.[].uuid] | unique | length) == 7)'
}
seed_persist_pin() {
    persist_parent=$seed_dir/volume/@agent_user
    persist_dir=$persist_parent/persist
    parent_pin=$(seed_member_pin "$persist_parent") || seed_fail "invalid persistence parent"
    [ -d "$persist_dir" ] && [ ! -L "$persist_dir" ] &&
        [ "$(stat -c %a "$persist_dir")" = 700 ] || seed_fail "unsafe ordinary persistence directory"
    ! btrfs subvolume show "$persist_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1 || seed_fail "persistence must not be a subvolume"
    ! mountpoint -q "$persist_dir" || seed_fail "persistence source must not be a separate mount"
    [ "$(stat -c %d "$persist_dir")" = "$(stat -c %d "$persist_parent")" ] || seed_fail "persistence is not on its parent filesystem"
    # The sprout FSID identifies the device set across remounts. Kernel st_dev
    # is checked against the parent live, never persisted as a reboot-stable ID.
    jq -cn --argjson parent "$parent_pin" --arg inode "$(stat -c %i "$persist_dir")" --arg fsid "$sprout_fsid" \
        '{path:"@agent_user/persist",parent:$parent,inode:$inode,fsid:$fsid}'
}
seed_verify_layout() {
    [ "$(seed_image_metadata | jq -cS .)" = "$(jq -cS '.image' "$seed_dir/state.json")" ] || seed_fail "pinned image metadata changed"
    actual_pins=$(seed_layout_pins) || seed_fail "invalid shared sibling layout"
    [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$actual_pins" | jq -cS .)" = "$(jq -cS '.members' "$seed_dir/state.json")" ] || seed_fail "shared sibling IDs or UUIDs changed"
    [ "$(seed_persist_pin | jq -cS .)" = "$(jq -cS '.persist' "$seed_dir/state.json")" ] || seed_fail "private persistence directory or parent identity changed"
    for sibling in @ @agent_memory @agent_rules @agent_shared @agent_skills @agent_soul @agent_user; do
        case "$sibling" in @agent_rules|@agent_shared|@agent_soul) readonly=true ;; *) readonly=false ;; esac
        [ "$(btrfs property get -ts "$seed_dir/volume/$sibling" ro)" = "ro=$readonly" ] || seed_fail "sibling protection changed: $sibling"
    done
}
seed_bind_member() {
    member_source=$1 member_root=$2 member_readonly=$3
    [ -d "$member_root" ] && [ ! -L "$member_root" ] || seed_fail "unsafe guest member target: $member_root"
    if ! mountpoint -q "$member_root"; then
        case "$mode" in
            seed-check|seed-lungs|seed-enable-boot) seed_fail "guest member mount missing: $member_root" ;;
            seed-down) return ;;

        [ -z "$(find "$member_root" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -print -quit)" ] || seed_fail "guest member target is not empty"

    fi

        [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$member_root" -o FSTYPE)" = btrfs ] &&
        [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$member_root" -o FSROOT)" = "/${member_source#"$seed_dir/volume/"}" ] || seed_fail "guest member mount source changed"
    case ",$(findmnt -rn -M "$member_root" -o VFS-OPTIONS)," in
        *,ro,*) [ "$member_readonly" = true ] || seed_fail "private member is mounted read-only" ;;
        *) [ "$member_readonly" = false ] || seed_fail "protected member is writable" ;;
    esac
}
seed_mount_guest() {
    seed_verify_volume
    seed_verify_layout
    guest=$seed_dir/volume/@
    [ -d "$guest/agent" ] && [ ! -L "$guest/agent" ] || seed_fail "guest agent parent is not an ordinary directory"
    if btrfs subvolume show "$guest/agent" >/dev/null 2>&1; then seed_fail "guest agent parent must not be a subvolume"; fi
    if mountpoint -q "$native_root"; then
        [ "$(stat -c '%d:%i' "$native_root")" = "$(stat -c '%d:%i' "$guest")" ] &&
            [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$native_root" -o FSTYPE)" = btrfs ] &&
            [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$native_root" -o FSROOT)" = /@ ] || seed_fail "unexpected guest-root mount"
    else
        case "$mode" in seed-check|seed-lungs|seed-enable-boot) seed_fail "guest-root mount missing" ;; esac
        seed_empty_native_root
        mount --bind "$guest" "$native_root"
    fi
    for member in memory rules shared skills soul user; do

1:#!/usr/bin/env bash
2:# Completed manual provisioning step: one sparse disk, root + upgrade partitions.
3:# Storage preparation only; identity registration and container startup are separate.
4:set -euo pipefail
5:fail() { printf 'prepare-instance-disk: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
6:usage() {
7:    cat <<'USAGE'
8:Usage:
9:  prepare-instance-disk create NAME [--root-gib N] [--upgrade-gib N]
10:  prepare-instance-disk inspect NAME
11:  prepare-instance-disk prepare NAME --seed-device /dev/disk/by-uuid/UUID
12:
13:Pool: /var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool (mounted @3tched-leaf-pool)
14:Image: NAME.img, sparse raw, GPT root + upgrade partitions
15:Defaults: 20 GiB root, remaining approximately 40 GiB upgrade.
16:Existing images are never adopted, repartitioned or overwritten by create.
17:inspect reads the image and reports its partition table; it does not modify it.
18:USAGE
19:}
20:[[ $# -gt 0 ]] || { usage; exit 2; }
21:case $1 in -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;; esac
22:[[ $# -ge 2 ]] || fail 'action and instance name required'
23:action=$1 name=$2
24:shift 2
25:[[ $action == create || $action == inspect || $action == prepare ]] || fail 'unknown action'
26:[[ $name =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,62}$ ]] || fail 'invalid instance name'
27:root_gib=20 upgrade_gib=40 seed_device=
28:while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
29:    [[ $action != inspect ]] || fail 'inspect takes no options'
30:    [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || fail "missing value for $1"
31:    case $1 in
32:        --root-gib) [[ $action == create ]] || fail 'size applies to create'; root_gib=$2 ;;
33:        --upgrade-gib) [[ $action == create ]] || fail 'size applies to create'; upgrade_gib=$2 ;;
34:        --seed-device) [[ $action == prepare ]] || fail 'seed applies to prepare'; seed_device=$2 ;;
35:        *) fail "unknown option: $1" ;;
36:    esac
37:    shift 2
38:done
39:[[ $(id -u) == 0 ]] || fail 'host root owns disk preparation'
40:for tool in qemu-img sfdisk jq findmnt realpath stat flock date sync; do
41:    command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || fail "missing $tool"
42:done
43:for size in "$root_gib" "$upgrade_gib"; do
44:    [[ $size =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,3}$ ]] && (( size <= 1024 )) || fail 'partition size must be 1 to 1024 GiB'
45:done
46:pool=/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool
47:[[ -d $pool && ! -L $pool && $(realpath -e "$pool") == "$pool" ]] || fail 'leaf pool is absent or noncanonical'
48:[[ $(findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSTYPE) == btrfs && $(findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSROOT) == /@3tched-leaf-pool ]] || fail 'expected mounted @3tched-leaf-pool; refusing a root-directory fallback'
49:[[ $(stat -c '%u %a' "$pool") == '0 700' ]] || fail 'leaf pool must be root-owned mode 0700'

51:if [[ $action == inspect ]]; then
52:    [[ -f $image && ! -L $image ]] || fail 'image is absent or not a regular file'
53:    qemu-img info -f raw --output=json "$image"
54:    sfdisk --json "$image"

56:fi
57:umask 077
58:receipt_root=$pool/.provisioning
59:[[ ! -L $receipt_root ]] || fail 'receipt directory is a symlink'
60:mkdir -p -- "$receipt_root"
61:[[ $(stat -c '%u %a' "$receipt_root") == '0 700' ]] || fail 'receipt directory must be root-owned mode 0700'
62:lock=$receipt_root/$name.lock
63:[[ ! -L $lock && ( ! -e $lock || -f $lock ) ]] || fail 'invalid instance lock'
64:exec 9>"$lock"
65:flock -n 9 || fail 'another preparation owns this instance'
66:receipt=$receipt_root/$name.json
67:if [[ $action == prepare ]]; then
68:    for tool in losetup blkid blockdev btrfs mkfs.btrfs mount umount rg sed install; do
69:        command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || fail "missing $tool"
70:    done
71:    [[ $seed_device == /dev/disk/by-uuid/* && -b $seed_device ]] || fail 'stable seed UUID path required'
72:    [[ -f $image && ! -L $image && -f $receipt && ! -L $receipt ]] || fail 'disk and creation receipt required'
73:    jq -e --arg image "$image" --arg name "$name" --arg inode "$(stat -c %i "$image")" \
74:        --argjson bytes "$(stat -c %s "$image")" \
75:        '.phase=="disk-partitioned" and .image==$image and .name==$name and
76:         .image_inode==$inode and .image_bytes==$bytes and .identity_registered==false' "$receipt" >/dev/null || fail 'not a fresh partitioned disk; never repeat device-add'
77:    table=$(sfdisk --json "$image")
78:    jq -e --argjson actual "$table" '.partition_table==$actual.partitiontable and
79:        (.partition_table.partitions|length)==2' "$receipt" >/dev/null || fail 'partition table differs from receipt'
80:    [[ -z $(losetup -j "$image") ]] || fail 'image already attached'
81:    seed_fsid=$(blkid -p -s UUID -o value "$seed_device")
82:    [[ $seed_device == /dev/disk/by-uuid/"$seed_fsid" ]] || fail 'seed UUID mismatch'
83:    btrfs inspect-internal dump-super "$seed_device" | sed -n '/flags/,/fsid/p' | rg -q SEEDING || fail 'seed is not sealed'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Completed manual provisioning step: one sparse disk, root + upgrade partitions.
# Storage preparation only; identity registration and container startup are separate.
set -euo pipefail
fail() { printf 'prepare-instance-disk: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
usage() {
    cat <<'USAGE'
Usage:
  prepare-instance-disk create NAME [--root-gib N] [--upgrade-gib N]
  prepare-instance-disk inspect NAME
  prepare-instance-disk prepare NAME --seed-device /dev/disk/by-uuid/UUID

Pool: /var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool (mounted @3tched-leaf-pool)
Image: NAME.img, sparse raw, GPT root + upgrade partitions
Defaults: 20 GiB root, remaining approximately 40 GiB upgrade.
Existing images are never adopted, repartitioned or overwritten by create.
inspect reads the image and reports its partition table; it does not modify it.
USAGE
}
[[ $# -gt 0 ]] || { usage; exit 2; }
case $1 in -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;; esac
[[ $# -ge 2 ]] || fail 'action and instance name required'
action=$1 name=$2
shift 2
[[ $action == create || $action == inspect || $action == prepare ]] || fail 'unknown action'
[[ $name =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,62}$ ]] || fail 'invalid instance name'
root_gib=20 upgrade_gib=40 seed_device=
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    [[ $action != inspect ]] || fail 'inspect takes no options'
    [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || fail "missing value for $1"
    case $1 in
        --root-gib) [[ $action == create ]] || fail 'size applies to create'; root_gib=$2 ;;
        --upgrade-gib) [[ $action == create ]] || fail 'size applies to create'; upgrade_gib=$2 ;;
        --seed-device) [[ $action == prepare ]] || fail 'seed applies to prepare'; seed_device=$2 ;;
        *) fail "unknown option: $1" ;;
    esac
    shift 2
done
[[ $(id -u) == 0 ]] || fail 'host root owns disk preparation'
for tool in qemu-img sfdisk jq findmnt realpath stat flock date sync; do
    command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || fail "missing $tool"
done
for size in "$root_gib" "$upgrade_gib"; do
    [[ $size =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,3}$ ]] && (( size <= 1024 )) || fail 'partition size must be 1 to 1024 GiB'
done
pool=/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool
[[ -d $pool && ! -L $pool && $(realpath -e "$pool") == "$pool" ]] || fail 'leaf pool is absent or noncanonical'
[[ $(findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSTYPE) == btrfs && $(findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSROOT) == /@3tched-leaf-pool ]] || fail 'expected mounted @3tched-leaf-pool; refusing a root-directory fallback'
[[ $(stat -c '%u %a' "$pool") == '0 700' ]] || fail 'leaf pool must be root-owned mode 0700'
image=$pool/$name.img
if [[ $action == inspect ]]; then
    [[ -f $image && ! -L $image ]] || fail 'image is absent or not a regular file'
    qemu-img info -f raw --output=json "$image"
    sfdisk --json "$image"
    exit 0
fi
umask 077
receipt_root=$pool/.provisioning
[[ ! -L $receipt_root ]] || fail 'receipt directory is a symlink'
mkdir -p -- "$receipt_root"
[[ $(stat -c '%u %a' "$receipt_root") == '0 700' ]] || fail 'receipt directory must be root-owned mode 0700'
lock=$receipt_root/$name.lock
[[ ! -L $lock && ( ! -e $lock || -f $lock ) ]] || fail 'invalid instance lock'
exec 9>"$lock"
flock -n 9 || fail 'another preparation owns this instance'
receipt=$receipt_root/$name.json
if [[ $action == prepare ]]; then
    for tool in losetup blkid blockdev btrfs mkfs.btrfs mount umount rg sed install; do
        command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || fail "missing $tool"
    done
    [[ $seed_device == /dev/disk/by-uuid/* && -b $seed_device ]] || fail 'stable seed UUID path required'
    [[ -f $image && ! -L $image && -f $receipt && ! -L $receipt ]] || fail 'disk and creation receipt required'
    jq -e --arg image "$image" --arg name "$name" --arg inode "$(stat -c %i "$image")" \
        --argjson bytes "$(stat -c %s "$image")" \
        '.phase=="disk-partitioned" and .image==$image and .name==$name and
         .image_inode==$inode and .image_bytes==$bytes and .identity_registered==false' "$receipt" >/dev/null || fail 'not a fresh partitioned disk; never repeat device-add'
    table=$(sfdisk --json "$image")
    jq -e --argjson actual "$table" '.partition_table==$actual.partitiontable and
        (.partition_table.partitions|length)==2' "$receipt" >/dev/null || fail 'partition table differs from receipt'
    [[ -z $(losetup -j "$image") ]] || fail 'image already attached'
    seed_fsid=$(blkid -p -s UUID -o value "$seed_device")
    [[ $seed_device == /dev/disk/by-uuid/"$seed_fsid" ]] || fail 'seed UUID mismatch'
    btrfs inspect-internal dump-super "$seed_device" | sed -n '/flags/,/fsid/p' | rg -q SEEDING || fail 'seed is not sealed'
    root_mount=$pool/.mounts/$name/root
    upgrade_mount=$pool/.mounts/$name/upgrade
    [[ ! -e $pool/.mounts/$name ]] || fail 'mount directory already exists'
    phase() {
        jq --arg phase "$1" '.phase=$phase' "$receipt" > "$receipt.new"
        mv -T "$receipt.new" "$receipt"
        sync -f "$receipt_root"
    }

    mkdir -p "$root_mount" "$upgrade_mount"
    blockdev --setro "$seed_device"
    seed_loop=$(losetup --find --show --read-only "$seed_device")
    disk_loop=$(losetup --find --show --partscan "$image")
    root_partition=${disk_loop}p1 upgrade_partition=${disk_loop}p2
    jq --arg seed "$seed_device" --arg sf "$seed_fsid" --arg sl "$seed_loop" --arg dl "$disk_loop" \
        --arg rp "$root_partition" --arg up "$upgrade_partition" --arg rm "$root_mount" --arg um "$upgrade_mount" \
        '.seed_device=$seed|.seed_fsid=$sf|.seed_loop=$sl|.disk_loop=$dl|
         .root_partition=$rp|.upgrade_partition=$up|.root_mount=$rm|.upgrade_mount=$um' "$receipt" > "$receipt.new"
    mv -T "$receipt.new" "$receipt"
    for partition in "$root_partition" "$upgrade_partition"; do
        [[ -b $partition && -z $(blkid -p -s TYPE -o value "$partition" || true) ]] || fail 'partition is not blank'
    done
    mount -o ro,subvolid=5 "$seed_loop" "$root_mount"
    for member in @ @agent_memory @agent_rules @agent_shared @agent_skills @agent_soul @agent_user; do
        btrfs subvolume show "$root_mount/$member" >/dev/null || fail "seed missing $member"
    done
    phase root-device-add-intent
    btrfs device add "$root_partition" "$root_mount"
    sync -f "$root_mount"
    umount "$root_mount"
    mount -o "rw,subvolid=5,device=$seed_loop,device=$root_partition" "$root_partition" "$root_mount"
    phase upgrade-format-intent
    mkfs.btrfs -L 3tched-upgrade "$upgrade_partition"
    mount -o rw,subvolid=5 "$upgrade_partition" "$upgrade_mount"
    btrfs subvolume create "$upgrade_mount/@"
    for member in @agent_memory @agent_rules @agent_skills @agent_user; do
        btrfs property set -ts "$root_mount/$member" ro false
    done
    for member in @agent_shared @agent_soul; do
        btrfs property set -ts "$root_mount/$member" ro true
    done
    install -d -m 0700 "$root_mount/@agent_user/persist"
    install -d -m 0755 "$root_mount/@/opt/run-mounts/persist"
    sync -f "$root_mount"
    sync -f "$upgrade_mount"
    jq --arg rf "$(blkid -p -s UUID -o value "$root_partition")" \
        --arg uf "$(blkid -p -s UUID -o value "$upgrade_partition")" \
        '.root_fsid=$rf|.upgrade_fsid=$uf|.filesystem_prepared=true|.phase="filesystems-prepared"' "$receipt" > "$receipt.new"
    mv -T "$receipt.new" "$receipt"
    sync -f "$receipt_root"
    printf 'Filesystems prepared; mounts retained for next manual step. Receipt: %s\n' "$receipt"
    exit 0
fi
[[ ! -e $image && ! -L $image ]] || fail 'image already exists; use inspect, never repeat creation'
receipt=$receipt_root/$name.json
[[ ! -e $receipt && ! -L $receipt ]] || fail 'retained preparation intent exists; inspect before any retry'
total_gib=$((root_gib + upgrade_gib))
created_at=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
jq -n --arg name "$name" --arg image "$image" --arg pool "$pool" --arg time "$created_at" \
    --argjson root "$root_gib" --argjson upgrade "$upgrade_gib" --argjson total "$total_gib" \
    '{version:1,layout:"raw-gpt-root-upgrade-v1",phase:"disk-create-intent",
      name:$name,image:$image,pool:$pool,created_at:$time,
      root_gib:$root,upgrade_gib_requested:$upgrade,total_gib:$total,
      identity_registered:false,filesystem_prepared:false}' > "$receipt"
# qemu-img creates a sparse raw disk; GPT/alignment overhead reduces partition 2
# slightly. All commands address only the newly created image, never a host disk.
qemu-img create -f raw "$image" "${total_gib}G"
chmod 0600 "$image"
sfdisk "$image" <<PARTITIONS
label: gpt
unit: sectors

size=${root_gib}G, type=L, name="3tched-root"
type=L, name="3tched-upgrade"
PARTITIONS
partition_table=$(sfdisk --json "$image")
# Pin partition identities now; loop numbers are runtime attachments, not owners.
jq --arg inode "$(stat -c %i "$image")" --argjson bytes "$(stat -c %s "$image")" \
    --argjson partition_table "$partition_table" \
    '.phase="disk-partitioned" | .image_inode=$inode | .image_bytes=$bytes |
     .partition_table=$partition_table.partitiontable' "$receipt" > "$receipt.new"
mv -T -- "$receipt.new" "$receipt"
sync -f "$pool"
printf 'Prepared disk: %s\nReceipt: %s\n' "$image" "$receipt"
printf '%s\n' 'No filesystems formatted, container created, seed attached, or Cozo binding committed.'

instance=$(incus query "/1.0/instances/$name")

   '.phase="root-bound"|.root_bound=true|.threetched_root=$root|.instance=$instance|

224:## 4. Why the seed contract needs block storage
…
243:
244:- A subvolume path is not the writable block member passed to `btrfs device add`.
245:- A writable snapshot of a read-only subvolume can isolate file changes, but **substituting it for a sprout changes the specified mechanism and proof model**.
246:- Keeping a backing file inside a subvolume still requires some block-device presentation for that file. Recording it in Cozo does not provide that presentation.
247:- A real non-loop block device can be added; a loop is an implementation choice, not a Btrfs requirement.

249:### Upgrade replica is a different issue
250:
251:Btrfs send/receive operates on subvolumes and snapshots. There is no general Btrfs requirement that an upgrade replica occupy a second partition.
252:

254:
255:> “All snapshots involved in one send command must be read-only…”
256:
257:and:
258:
259:> “Read-only mount of the subvolume is not sufficient…”
260:
261:The receive documentation also requires protecting the receive destination against concurrent modification until reception completes.
262:

Replacing that with a custom filesystem subvolume requires an explicit proof/schema migration, not a path substitution.

275:> “Before v6.17 kernel, a seed device could have been mounted independently along with sprouted filesystems. But since 6.17 kernel, a seed device can only be mounted either through a sprouted filesystem, or the seed device itself, not both at the same time.”
276:
277:Its reason:
278:
279:> “This is to ensure a block device to have only a single filesystem bound to it, so that runtime device missing events can be properly handled.”
280:
281:Source: [Btrfs seeding-device documentation](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Seeding-device.html).

## 4. Why the seed contract needs block storage
…

- A subvolume path is not the writable block member passed to `btrfs device add`.
- A writable snapshot of a read-only subvolume can isolate file changes, but **substituting it for a sprout changes the specified mechanism and proof model**.
- Keeping a backing file inside a subvolume still requires some block-device presentation for that file. Recording it in Cozo does not provide that presentation.
- A real non-loop block device can be added; a loop is an implementation choice, not a Btrfs requirement.

### Upgrade replica is a different issue

Btrfs send/receive operates on subvolumes and snapshots. There is no general Btrfs requirement that an upgrade replica occupy a second partition.

Upstream says:

> “All snapshots involved in one send command must be read-only…”

and:

> “Read-only mount of the subvolume is not sufficient…”

The receive documentation also requires protecting the receive destination against concurrent modification until reception completes.

Sources: [btrfs-send](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs-send.html), [btrfs-receive](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs-receive.html).

**However, the supplied implementation currently requires more than that general primitive:** its V4 proof requires a separate upgrade filesystem, top-level mount, a single-device filesystem, GPT geometry, and a loop-backed second partition. Replacing that with a custom filesystem subvolume requires an explicit proof/schema migration, not a path substitution.

Citation: `evidence/source/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/identity_clean_provision/partitioned.rs:109-138`.

---

## 5. Kernel 6.17+ and the permanent seed mount

The upstream caveat is exact:

> “Before v6.17 kernel, a seed device could have been mounted independently along with sprouted filesystems. But since 6.17 kernel, a seed device can only be mounted either through a sprouted filesystem, or the seed device itself, not both at the same time.”

Its reason:

> “This is to ensure a block device to have only a single filesystem bound to it, so that runtime device missing events can be properly handled.”

Source: [Btrfs seeding-device documentation](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Seeding-device.html).

This applies directly to the **same-block-device** interpretation of the supplied 6.18 receipt and permanent standalone mount requirement.

It does **not** authorize:

- Unmounting the permanent seed.
- Clearing its seeding flag.
- Removing the seed from sprouts.
- Rebuilding/copying the seed.
- Downgrading or modifying the kernel.
- Assuming that aliases preserve supported sharing semantics.

The documentation itself warns that clearing the seeding flag and changing the seed invalidates existing dependent filesystems.

The contemporary maintainer discussion also explicitly discusses only one sprout mount at a time on the same device, but is a discussion rather than proof of every alias topology.  
Source: [August 2025 upstream filesystem discussion](https://www.spinics.net/lists/linux-fsdevel/msg309379.html).

**Do not combine the generic multi-sprout example with the version caveat to claim unrestricted concurrent same-device mounting on 6.18. Conversely, do not turn the caveat into an unsupported impossibility claim about every distinct block-view implementation.**

---

## 6. What actually worked historically—and what differs now

### October 5: native Incus plus external sprout construction

Historical `op-identity-root` creates distinct read-only seed loops and writable leaf loops:

```sh
seed_view=$(losetup --find --show --read-only --loop-ref "seed:$native_uuid" "$seed_device")
```

```sh
leaf_loop=$(losetup --find --show --loop-ref "leaf:$native_uuid" "$leaf")
```

It then performs:

```sh
btrfs device add "$leaf_loop" "$seed_dir/volume"
```

and binds the prepared filesystem root:

```sh
mount --bind "$guest" "$native_root"
```

Citations:

- `evidence/history/oct05-admission-helper/deploy/runit/libexec-3tched/op-identity-root:1003-1024`
- Same file `:1104-1124`
- Same file `:1147-1198`

It explicitly rejects a standalone physical-source mount:

> `directly mounted seed source; unmount it and keep its fstab entry noauto`

Citation: same file `:494-505`.

**Conclusion:** strong evidence that native Incus and sprouts were integrated, but this historical implementation violates the latest no-host-loops constraint and conflicts with the standalone permanent-mount requirement.

### October 11: upgrade-over-seed read-only root

The historical binder contains:

```sh
mount --bind -o ro,X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$root/@" "$seed_layer"
mount --bind -o ro,X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$replica/@" "$upgrade_layer"
mount -t overlay overlay -o "ro,lowerdir=$upgrade_layer:$seed_layer" "$view"
mount --bind "$view" "$container_root"
```

Citation: `evidence/history/oct11-start/deploy/scripts/bind-instance-root.sh:82-85`.

Important distinctions:

- Upgrade is the higher-priority **lower**.
- The other lower is the sprout’s inherited `@`.

These are **proposed changes**, not implemented functionality or a proven feasible deployment.

### A. Preserve the existing native/identity control plane

- Bootstrap and model routing remain out of scope; do not activate `jev-router`.

### B. Change proof representation, not its strength

Target existing files:

1. **`identity_clean_provision.rs`**
   - Replace image-only assumptions in the selected no-loop layout: `<name>.img`, leaf inode/size as regular-file identity, mandatory GPT partition geometry.

   - Update the existing plan author and Cozo version predicates together.
   - Do not broaden fresh/replacement eligibility or relax unknown-field rejection.

2. **`storage.rs`**
   - Replace `LOOP_GET_STATUS64` backing-file equivalence with an equally strong held-descriptor proof for the selected real storage primitive.
   - For a direct-block seed/sprout design, prove the actual protected seed block object and actual writable member, their kernel identities, FSIDs and access modes, and reject loop-backed ancestry.

3. **`partitioned.rs`**
   - Replace image/loop partition ownership checks only where the selected layout actually eliminates GPT/image backing.
   - If physical partitions remain, retain genuine partition-parent/geometry/identity proof without requiring a loop parent.
   - If separate storage objects replace the two partitions, explicitly prove separation and each object’s ownership; do not fabricate PARTUUID/GPT fields.
   - Preserve readonly overlay lower order, ID-mapped source equality, paired generation receipt, received/host UUID ancestry and protected baselines.

4. **Cozo `clean_provision.rs`**
   - Extend only the recognized provenance-layout validation needed for the actual selected storage representation.
   - Preserve complete predecessor equality, deterministic digest operation, replay equality and immutable completed binding.
   - No new public API or direct database mutation is needed for the specification.

### C. Modify the existing external helper chain coherently

The document identifies the necessary existing integration targets:

- `prepare-instance-disk.sh`: remove image/loop allocation only after selecting a genuine replacement primitive and receipt.
- `provision-workspace-subscriber.sh`: retain existing staged workflow and original native operation; carry the selected storage receipt consistently.
- `sync-instance-upgrade.sh`: retain pre-receive mount/FSID proof, host→container pairing, incremental ancestry, stopped-only lower-layer changes and complete restoration.

These shell modification targets are derived from the fully read source document and reports; their full implementation audit belongs to the parent’s shell-source work.

### D. Explicit unresolved requirement conflict

The Incus skill read in this session states:

> “Btrfs seeding/sprouting | Separate block-device filesystem operation; a subvolume is not a writable block member for `btrfs device add`.”

The source document says:

> “The filesystem stage attaches a read-only loop view of the sealed seed and adds the blank root partition once as its writable leaf. It inherits the seven seed subvolumes; it does not copy the root or create replacement agent subvolumes.”

`shared-seed-provisioning.md:44–47`.

It also says:

> “Linux 6.17 and newer cannot mount the standalone seed and a sprouted filesystem simultaneously; the host mount owner must reconcile the standalone seed mount and its boot declaration before pairing.”

`shared-seed-provisioning.md:21–24`.

Consequences:

- **Established:** simply changing to Incus-managed subvolumes does not satisfy the current seed-member proof.
- **Established:** current image/seed wrappers and pool image violate the hard no-host-loops rule.
- **[INFERENCE] Conditional direction:** actual non-loop writable block storage could retain block-level seeding semantics, without a disk image, if a supported available allocation and mounting arrangement is established.
- **Not established:** that such an arrangement is available, supports the required concurrent/permanent seed mounts on the deployed kernel, or can be adopted through the exact existing Incus storage owner without prohibited changes.
- **Not acceptable:** copied roots, ordinary snapshots or an overlay upper silently presented as the original writable sprout.

## 4. Why the seed contract needs block storage
…

- A subvolume path is not the writable block member passed to `btrfs device add`.
- A writable snapshot of a read-only subvolume can isolate file changes, but **substituting it for a sprout changes the specified mechanism and proof model**.
- Keeping a backing file inside a subvolume still requires some block-device presentation for that file. Recording it in Cozo does not provide that presentation.
- A real non-loop block device can be added; a loop is an implementation choice, not a Btrfs requirement.

### Upgrade replica is a different issue

Btrfs send/receive operates on subvolumes and snapshots. There is no general Btrfs requirement that an upgrade replica occupy a second partition.

Upstream says:

> “All snapshots involved in one send command must be read-only…”

and:

> “Read-only mount of the subvolume is not sufficient…”

The receive documentation also requires protecting the receive destination against concurrent modification until reception completes.

Sources: [btrfs-send](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs-send.html), [btrfs-receive](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs-receive.html).

**However, the supplied implementation currently requires more than that general primitive:** its V4 proof requires a separate upgrade filesystem, top-level mount, a single-device filesystem, GPT geometry, and a loop-backed second partition. Replacing that with a custom filesystem subvolume requires an explicit proof/schema migration, not a path substitution.

Citation: `evidence/source/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/identity_clean_provision/partitioned.rs:109-138`.

---

## 5. Kernel 6.17+ and the permanent seed mount

The upstream caveat is exact:

> “Before v6.17 kernel, a seed device could have been mounted independently along with sprouted filesystems. But since 6.17 kernel, a seed device can only be mounted either through a sprouted filesystem, or the seed device itself, not both at the same time.”

Its reason:

> “This is to ensure a block device to have only a single filesystem bound to it, so that runtime device missing events can be properly handled.”

Source: [Btrfs seeding-device documentation](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Seeding-device.html).

This applies directly to the **same-block-device** interpretation of the supplied 6.18 receipt and permanent standalone mount requirement.

It does **not** authorize:

- Unmounting the permanent seed.
- Clearing its seeding flag.
- Removing the seed from sprouts.
- Rebuilding/copying the seed.
- Downgrading or modifying the kernel.
- Assuming that aliases preserve supported sharing semantics.

The documentation itself warns that clearing the seeding flag and changing the seed invalidates existing dependent filesystems.

The contemporary maintainer discussion also explicitly discusses only one sprout mount at a time on the same device, but is a discussion rather than proof of every alias topology.  
Source: [August 2025 upstream filesystem discussion](https://www.spinics.net/lists/linux-fsdevel/msg309379.html).

**Do not combine the generic multi-sprout example with the version caveat to claim unrestricted concurrent same-device mounting on 6.18. Conversely, do not turn the caveat into an unsupported impossibility claim about every distinct block-view implementation.**

---

## 6. What actually worked historically—and what differs now

### October 5: native Incus plus external sprout construction

Historical `op-identity-root` creates distinct read-only seed loops and writable leaf loops:

```sh
seed_view=$(losetup --find --show --read-only --loop-ref "seed:$native_uuid" "$seed_device")
```

```sh
leaf_loop=$(losetup --find --show --loop-ref "leaf:$native_uuid" "$leaf")
```

It then performs:

```sh
btrfs device add "$leaf_loop" "$seed_dir/volume"
```

and binds the prepared filesystem root:

```sh
mount --bind "$guest" "$native_root"
```

Citations:

- `evidence/history/oct05-admission-helper/deploy/runit/libexec-3tched/op-identity-root:1003-1024`
- Same file `:1104-1124`
- Same file `:1147-1198`

It explicitly rejects a standalone physical-source mount:

> `directly mounted seed source; unmount it and keep its fstab entry noauto`

Citation: same file `:494-505`.

**Conclusion:** strong evidence that native Incus and sprouts were integrated, but this historical implementation violates the latest no-host-loops constraint and conflicts with the standalone permanent-mount requirement.

### October 11: upgrade-over-seed read-only root

The historical binder contains:

```sh
mount --bind -o ro,X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$root/@" "$seed_layer"
mount --bind -o ro,X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$replica/@" "$upgrade_layer"
mount -t overlay overlay -o "ro,lowerdir=$upgrade_layer:$seed_layer" "$view"
mount --bind "$view" "$container_root"
```

Citation: `evidence/history/oct11-start/deploy/scripts/bind-instance-root.sh:82-85`.

Important distinctions:

- Upgrade is the higher-priority **lower**.
- The other lower is the sprout’s inherited `@`.
- Root is read-only.
- There is no writable OverlayFS `upperdir`/`workdir`.
- Persistent identity writes live in separately bound inherited siblings and `@agent_user/persist`.

The supplied historical handoff states:

> “Canonical identity_sled.touch_session completed: 3tchedChatbot Running, PID11719.”

It also explicitly limits the persistence claim:

> “Boot wiring is deployed; actual reboot/cold-sync path unexercised…”

Citation: `evidence/context/HANDOFF.md:5940-5962`.

Citations:

## 4. Why the seed contract needs block storage
…

- A subvolume path is not the writable block member passed to `btrfs device add`.
- A writable snapshot of a read-only subvolume can isolate file changes, but **substituting it for a sprout changes the specified mechanism and proof model**.
- Keeping a backing file inside a subvolume still requires some block-device presentation for that file. Recording it in Cozo does not provide that presentation.
- A real non-loop block device can be added; a loop is an implementation choice, not a Btrfs requirement.

### Upgrade replica is a different issue

Btrfs send/receive operates on subvolumes and snapshots. There is no general Btrfs requirement that an upgrade replica occupy a second partition.

Upstream says:

> “All snapshots involved in one send command must be read-only…”

and:

> “Read-only mount of the subvolume is not sufficient…”

The receive documentation also requires protecting the receive destination against concurrent modification until reception completes.

Sources: [btrfs-send](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs-send.html), [btrfs-receive](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs-receive.html).

**However, the supplied implementation currently requires more than that general primitive:** its V4 proof requires a separate upgrade filesystem, top-level mount, a single-device filesystem, GPT geometry, and a loop-backed second partition. Replacing that with a custom filesystem subvolume requires an explicit proof/schema migration, not a path substitution.

Citation: `evidence/source/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/identity_clean_provision/partitioned.rs:109-138`.

---

## 5. Kernel 6.17+ and the permanent seed mount

The upstream caveat is exact:

> “Before v6.17 kernel, a seed device could have been mounted independently along with sprouted filesystems. But since 6.17 kernel, a seed device can only be mounted either through a sprouted filesystem, or the seed device itself, not both at the same time.”

Its reason:

> “This is to ensure a block device to have only a single filesystem bound to it, so that runtime device missing events can be properly handled.”

Source: [Btrfs seeding-device documentation](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Seeding-device.html).

This applies directly to the **same-block-device** interpretation of the supplied 6.18 receipt and permanent standalone mount requirement.

It does **not** authorize:

- Unmounting the permanent seed.
- Clearing its seeding flag.
- Removing the seed from sprouts.
- Rebuilding/copying the seed.
- Downgrading or modifying the kernel.
- Assuming that aliases preserve supported sharing semantics.

The documentation itself warns that clearing the seeding flag and changing the seed invalidates existing dependent filesystems.

The contemporary maintainer discussion also explicitly discusses only one sprout mount at a time on the same device, but is a discussion rather than proof of every alias topology.  
Source: [August 2025 upstream filesystem discussion](https://www.spinics.net/lists/linux-fsdevel/msg309379.html).

**Do not combine the generic multi-sprout example with the version caveat to claim unrestricted concurrent same-device mounting on 6.18. Conversely, do not turn the caveat into an unsupported impossibility claim about every distinct block-view implementation.**

---

## 6. What actually worked historically—and what differs now

### October 5: native Incus plus external sprout construction

Historical `op-identity-root` creates distinct read-only seed loops and writable leaf loops:

```sh
seed_view=$(losetup --find --show --read-only --loop-ref "seed:$native_uuid" "$seed_device")
```

```sh
leaf_loop=$(losetup --find --show --loop-ref "leaf:$native_uuid" "$leaf")
```

It then performs:

```sh
btrfs device add "$leaf_loop" "$seed_dir/volume"
```

and binds the prepared filesystem root:

```sh
mount --bind "$guest" "$native_root"
```

Citations:

- `evidence/history/oct05-admission-helper/deploy/runit/libexec-3tched/op-identity-root:1003-1024`
- Same file `:1104-1124`
- Same file `:1147-1198`

It explicitly rejects a standalone physical-source mount:

> `directly mounted seed source; unmount it and keep its fstab entry noauto`

Citation: same file `:494-505`.

**Conclusion:** strong evidence that native Incus and sprouts were integrated, but this historical implementation violates the latest no-host-loops constraint and conflicts with the standalone permanent-mount requirement.

### October 11: upgrade-over-seed read-only root

The historical binder contains:

```sh
mount --bind -o ro,X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$root/@" "$seed_layer"
mount --bind -o ro,X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$replica/@" "$upgrade_layer"
mount -t overlay overlay -o "ro,lowerdir=$upgrade_layer:$seed_layer" "$view"
mount --bind "$view" "$container_root"
```

Important distinctions:

- Upgrade is the higher-priority **lower**.
- The other lower is the sprout’s inherited `@`.
- Root is read-only.
- There is no writable OverlayFS `upperdir`/`workdir`.
- Persistent identity writes live in separately bound inherited siblings and `@agent_user/persist`.

The supplied historical handoff states:

> “Canonical identity_sled.touch_session completed: 3tchedChatbot Running, PID11719.”

It also explicitly limits the persistence claim:
